Summary adjusted using the Financial Stability Report (FSR):
- The FOMC kept policy highly accommodative (0–0.25% federal funds rate; ongoing asset purchases of $80B Treasuries and $40B agency MBS per month) to support maximum employment and 2% average inflation goals.
- Economic activity and employment have strengthened on vaccinations and policy support, but sectors hit hardest by the pandemic remain weak; inflation pressures are seen as largely transitory.
- The FSR notes overall financial conditions are accommodative and policy measures supported market functioning and credit flow, but it also highlights elevated vulnerabilities—particularly high asset valuations, pockets of business leverage, and structural fragilities in short‑term funding markets—leaving risks to the outlook.
- Banks remain well capitalized and liquid, which mitigates some stability risks, but the course of the virus and reopening dynamics remain key uncertainties.

Net effect on sentiment: modestly positive but tempered by elevated financial vulnerabilities and ongoing pandemic-related risks.
